_comment: The Studio routing table (machine-readable). Source: codex-claude-paperclip-model-routing-research.md sections 4, 6, 7 and 8, Benjamin's source of truth. Every route is a starting hypothesis until measured (research 7.2); the usage-cap ledger records each agent's measured cost per run. The Director and Principal read skills/routing-table/SKILL.md, which is generated from the same decisions. Changing an agent's model, adding an agent or making a planned agent active needs Benjamin's approval.

Clerk.use: polling, gates, CI and check status, diffs, counts, cost and usage reports

Worker.use: bounded jobs from qwen/jobs with a passing golden set (qwen-job skill); no cloud usage

Scout.use: exhaustive but bounded doing: repo inventories, evidence collection, extraction beyond the Worker's context; returns an evidence packet

Codex-Scout.use: same work as Scout, on the Codex allowance

Liaison.use: client and Board drafts, the question register

Recorder.use: journals, metrics and lessons in the Studio repo

Builder-1.use: routine and multi-file implementation, UI, SEO, docs, tests

Codex-Builder.use: implementation baseline on the Codex allowance: routine and multi-file changes, reviews

Principal.use: high-risk engineering, difficult debugging, qualified independent review

Codex-Principal.use: hard judgement and difficult failures on the Codex allowance; independent review of Claude-built high-risk work

Architect.use: Studio architecture review after a production phase (architect-review skill); rare

Director.use: plans, task packets, routing, acceptance, disputes; never implementation

caps._note: Enforced by bin/studio-quota in agent-exec (policy/quota.json). Never add Claude and Codex percentages together; a route that saves Claude by spending spare Codex allowance raises throughput without being 'cheaper'.

routes.examples: checks, counts, inventories of files, clerical totals, exit codes
summaries, exact quotes, classification into known categories, dedupe, inbox triage
routes.escalate_when: input exceeds the job's limit, the job is not enabled, or the Worker hands it back
routes.accept: schema and source checks (the job's own checks)

routes.examples: repo inventory, 'find every place that', dependency audit, evidence collection across many files
routes.escalate_when: coverage gaps or contradictions the scout cannot resolve
routes.accept: evidence packet with a coverage manifest; the requester checks high-risk findings at the source

routes.examples: phase plans, trade-offs, acceptance criteria, stack decisions
routes.escalate_when: a consequential or ambiguous decision: Board
routes.accept: explicit trade-offs and acceptance criteria; B plans need Benjamin's approval

routes.examples: a change following an established pattern, copy edits, config, small fixes
routes.escalate_when: the change stops being routine or leaves its allowed paths
routes.accept: targeted tests, make check, diff within allowed paths

routes.examples: a feature or integration across several files
routes.escalate_when: uncertain contracts, state or failure handling
routes.accept: tests for the new behaviour, make check, relevant review

routes.examples: page styling, responsive layout, visual polish
routes.escalate_when: the look is not decided (that is Benjamin's), or rendered evidence fails
routes.accept: screenshots at phone and desktop width, interaction check, axe; a passing build alone is not enough

routes.examples: unfamiliar root cause, migration, incident diagnosis, repeated red checks
routes.escalate_when: no evidence-backed diagnosis after one bounded attempt: Director
routes.accept: a reproduced cause and a test that fails before the fix

routes.examples: auth, payments, permissions, refunds, data loss, security settings
routes.escalate_when: any change to approval class, spending, data handling or customer policy
routes.accept: risk-specific tests, independent review by a different agent, rollback evidence

routes.examples: routine reply to Terrie or a client
routes.escalate_when: commitments, prices, policy or anything ambiguous: Director, then Board
routes.accept: verified facts; sending needs an accepted human-only confirmation

routes.examples: 'done' on any B or high-risk task
routes.accept: deterministic evidence plus a qualified reviewer who is not the author; incomplete while checks are missing

rules.choose_provider: Among the first-route agents that are active, prefer the provider with more headroom in the digest's Usage line; never route to a planned agent. Do not pick a stronger model because the task is long; pick by uncertainty and consequence.
rules.retry: One bounded correction for a clear, local error. The same failure again means diagnosis or escalation, never a third try. Transport failures (network, rate limits) are retried with backoff and logged separately.
rules.parallel: Parallelise only independent work with stable interfaces, each in its own worktree; keep dependent schema, API and implementation work in order.
rules.no_subagents: Agents do not start sub-agents (Constitution). Delegation is a Paperclip subtask with its own packet, so it is capped, attributed and visible.
